Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC so we can get infra reserved and timelines locked in.

Call recap / success criteria (as discussed):
- Integration: Redwood API integrated with Acme's agent pipeline (simple REST calls).
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 300ms for single-turn customer prompts at 1k concurrent users (see notes below).
- Cost: Token/unit cost analysis completed and baseline throughput measured.
- Quality: Model outputs meet the QA prompt set pass rate >= 92% (we'll share the prompt set).

POC scope & timeline:
- 3-week POC starting the week of Aug 10 (target dates configurable)
- Week 1: Integration + test harness + baseline tests
- Week 2: Load tests, KV/prefix caching enabled, quantization profile evaluation
- Week 3: Final regression eval, handover + deployment runbook

Capacity ask (initial):
- Reserved capacity: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated) for the first 2 weeks, with the ability to scale to 6 GPUs for load tests/bursts.
- Autoscaling policy: target CPU/GPU utilization target 70% with step-scaling + buffer of 20% for unexpected spikes.
- Burst expectation: short bursts up to 6 GPUs, sustained for up to 2 hours during peak load tests.

Owner / contacts:
- Redwood AE: Marissa Cole (me) — project owner for schedule and commercial
- Redwood SE: Vivek Kulkarni — technical lead for infra and tests
- Acme technical lead: Jordan Lee (copied)

Attachments: draft proposal + sample capacity snapshot attached for your review.

Next steps:
1) Jordan / Sana — confirm the proposed start week (week of Aug 10) and whether the reserved capacity numbers look feasible on your side.
2) Vivek and Jordan to set a quick 30-minute infra sync (propose Aug 3/4).
3) I'll push a refined Statement of Work and contract redline once start date is confirmed.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side after reviewing the notes and the attached snapshot: 

1) Reserved GPUs: 4 A100-equiv for baseline seems reasonable. We may need a short runway to provision dedicated instances; can Redwood support a soft-start where we run on shared capacity for the first 48 hours while the reserved pool is provisioned?

2) Burst profile: We can accommodate bursts to 6 GPUs for 2 hours during scheduled load windows. For unscheduled bursts, we'll need autoscaling to handle short spikes (up to 10 minutes) without throttling user-facing calls. Can you confirm Redwood's minimum scale-up latency for an extra GPU?

3) Metrics: we'll provide the QA prompt set by EOD Thu (Jul 30). Can Vivek confirm the exact logging/trace fields Redwood needs for quality/regression tracking?

4) Start date: Aug 10 works for our internal stakeholders, but we'd prefer the infra sync on Aug 4 (Tue) 10:00am PT. Does that work for your team?

Jordan — great questions, answers below. Vivek looping in technical details.

1) Soft-start on shared capacity: Yes — Redwood can support a soft-start on hosted/shared capacity for the first 48 hours while we warm up the reserved pool. Performance characteristics will be slightly different during that window (~P95 will be higher by ~30-50ms), but it's a common pattern. We'll flag any baseline comparisons accordingly.

2) Scale-up latency: With our Dedicated offering, adding a hot GPU to the reserved pool typically completes within ~4-6 minutes (cold provisioning can be longer). For autoscaling we recommend proactive warm pools (pre-warmed instances) to keep scale-up under 90s for most bursts; we can enable that for the POC.

3) Logging/trace fields: Vivek — what we need from Acme: request_id, user_id (hashed), model_version, prompt_id, tokens_in/tokens_out, latency_ms, error_code, and an optional quality_label field for human QA results. If you can share your logging format, we'll map fields in our ingestion.

4) Autoscaling policy (proposed):
- Target utilization: 70% GPU utilization
- Scale step: +1 GPU when >75% for 3 minutes
- Max burst: 6 GPUs (manual/automatic for scheduled windows)
- Pre-warmed pool: 1 GPU maintained as hot spare during the POC

5) Ownership & runbook:
- Redwood SE (Vivek) will own test harness setup and metrics dashboard
- Acme infra (Jordan) to provide access and a test token + sample workload

I'll update the SOW to reflect the soft-start + pre-warmed pool and send for your review.
